uncited: When the mesh is deformed via a deformation function $\text{Deform}(\cdot)$ (e.g., skeletal animation), the posed position is $\mu_{pose} = \text{Deform}(\mu_{cano})$ [Parent].
The posed rotation $q_{pose}$ and scale $s_{pose}$ are derived from mesh attributes to maintain coherence [Parent].
Specifically, the rotation is interpolated from per-vertex quaternions, and scale is proportional to the area change of the embedded triangle relative to the canonical state [Parent].

*   **Cross-Triangle Handling:** As noted in the parent [Mesh-embedded representation](12559-mesh-embedded-representation.md), if optimization moves an embedding point across a triangle boundary, the embedding must be re-expressed in the neighboring triangle to maintain differentiability [Parent, S2].
Failure to handle this causes Gaussians to stick to boundaries and pile up [Parent].
